texts.preamble: K.Jothi vs The Secretary To Government on 18 November, 2020 Author: R.Hemalatha Bench: M. Sathyanarayanan, R.Hemalatha WP.No.1 In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras Dated 18.11.2020 Coram The Honourable Mr. Justice M. Sathyanarayanan And The Honourable Mrs. Justice R.Hemalatha WP.No.15392 of 2020 and W.M.P.No.19250 of 2020 K.Jothi .. Petitio Versus 1.The Secretary to Government Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department Government of Tamil Nadu St.George Fort, Secretariat, Chennai 600 009. 2.The Commissioner, Corporation of Chennai, Rippon Buildings, Chennai 600 003. http://www.judis.nic.in Wp 3.The Chairperson / Zonal Officer/ Executive Engineer (Zone-13) Township Vending Committee, Corporation of Chennai, No.115, Dr.Muthulakshmi Salai, Adayar, Chennai 600020. .. Res K.Jothi vs The Secretary To Government on 18 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84064600/ 1 Prayer:- Writ petition has been filed under Article 226 of the Con of India praying for the issuance of Writ of Mandamus to forbearin respondent 2 and 3, its officials, servants, agents or anybody und from inteferring with the running of the Petitoners Bunk Shop at N Sathiya Dev Avenue, near Open Park, Opposite to Cee Bros, chennai- wherein selling Tea, Coffee, Snacks, food and other items, till th of Appeal Committee Under Section 20 of the ''Street Vendors (Prot of Livelihood Regulation) Act, 2014''. For Petitioner : Mr.L.Chandrakumar For Respondents : Mr.R.Vijayakumar for R1 & R3 Mr.Raja Srinivas for R2 Order
texts.facts: The petitioner, on an earlier occasion, filed W.P.No.14282 of 2020, against the very same official respondents, praying for Writ of Certiorarified Mandamus to call for the records relating to the proceedings of the 3rd respondent dated 23.09.2020 and quash the same and consequently forbear http://www.judis.nic.in the respondents 2 and 3, from interfering with the running of the petitioner's bunk shop at No.174, Sathiya Dev Avenue, near Open Part, opposite to Cee Bros, Chennai 600 028, wherein he is selling tea, coffee, snacks, food and other items. The Writ Petition was taken up for final disposal on 09.10.2020 and having noted that the provisions of Sub-Section 3 of Section 18 of the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulations of Street Vending) Act, 2014, have not been adhered to, this Court has directed the Zonal Officer, Zone-13, Adyar, Chennai 600 020, to desist action for a period of thirty days from 25.09.2020 and thereafter, proceed strictly in accordance with law and the Writ Petition came to be disposed of accordingly. Now the writ petitioner came forward to file this present Writ Petition to forbear the respondents from any way interfere with the running of the petitioner's bunk shop till the formation of Appeal Committee under Section 20 of the said Act.
texts.arguments: 2. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that a batch of writ petition has been filed before this Court in W.P.No.32329 of 2020 batch etc., challenging the declaration of non vending zone in Egmore http://www.judis.nic.in area, especially Pantheon Road and Monteith Road and as such, the petitioner may be given a suitable alternative accommodation in the place of choice of the Corporation of Chennai and prays for appropriate orders. 3. Per contra, learned standing counsel appearing for the respondents 2 and 3 would submit that the petitioner has also been vacated from the Bunk Shop in question and admittedly, he is an encroacher and as a matter of right, he cannot seek for alternative accommodation and when the Writ Petition in W.P.No.32329 of 2020 batch etc., decides in favour of the petitioners therein, the petitioner may work out his remedy in accordance with law and prays for dismissal of this Writ Petition with exemplary costs, as it is an abuse of process of Court. The only point urged by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner is that in the light of declaration of non-vending zone in Egmore area, W.P.No.32329 of 2020 has been filed and the same is pending and till the disposal of the same, by taking into consideration the plight of the petitioner, suitable accommodation may be provided to him.

Per contra, learned standing counsel appearing for the respondents 2 and 3 would submit that the petitioner has also been vacated from the Bunk Shop in question and admittedly, he is an encroacher and as a matter of right, he cannot seek for alternative accommodation and when the Writ Petition in W.P.No.32329 of 2020 batch etc., decides in favour of the petitioners therein, the petitioner may work out his remedy in accordance with law and prays for dismissal of this Writ Petition with exemplary costs, as it is an abuse of process of Court. The only point urged by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner is that in the light of declaration of non-vending zone in Egmore area, W.P.No.32329 of 2020 has been filed and the same is pending and till the disposal of the same, by taking into consideration the plight of the petitioner, suitable accommodation may be provided to him.
